heroText: Helsingborg works best as a base in Sweden when you anchor days around Karnan, Sofiero Palace and Dunkers kulturhus. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Malmö Sturup Airport (MMX) handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.text: From 1429 Eric of Pomerania introduced the Sound Dues, a levy on all trading vessels passing through the sound between Helsingør and Helsingborg.
King Charles X Gustav of Sweden landed here on 5 March 1658 to take personal possession of the Scanian lands and was met by a delegation led by the bishop of the Diocese of Lund, Peder Winstrup.
The last Danish attempt to regain Scania was in 1710, when 14,000 men landed on the shores near Helsingborg.

On 20 October 1811, Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte, Marshal of France and crown prince-elect of Sweden (later King Charles XIV John) took his first step on Swedish soil in Helsingborg on his journey from Paris to Stockholm.
A tramway network was inaugurated in 1903 and closed down in 1967.
Following the Swedish orthography reform of 1906, the spelling of many place names in Sweden was modernized.
In 1912, it was decided to use the form Hälsingborg.
Adolf Hitler had ordered that all Danish Jews were to be arrested and deported to the concentration camps on Rosh HaShanah, the Jewish New Year which fell on 2 October 1943.

In preparation for the local government reform in 1971, Hälsingborg city council proposed that the new, enlarged municipality should be spelled Helsingborg; this form was adopted by the government of Sweden from 1 January 1971.
